query:
The family has a norm that everyone comes home for Christmas. Does this apply to all family members?

Options:
A. Dad
B. Imogen
C. Kofi
D. Mum
context:
[1] (about=Mum, episodic, t5 @2025-07-28T18:02:00) Right, Christmas! Everyone home, yes? I'll do the full works. Kofi, booked your flights? 🎄🙏
[2] (about=Mum, episodic, t6 @2025-07-28T22:58:00) Oh Kofi 😭😭😭 but we said everyone. It won't be the same without you. Are you sure?
[3] (about=Dad, core, t6 @2025-07-28T22:51:00) Don't build Christmas around airline pricing; we'll cope
[4] (about=Imogen, episodic, t6 @2025-07-28T23:04:00) Mum let him figure it out, flights are genuinely a lot. Kofi we'll do a video call Christmas morning either way 💙
[5] (about=Kofi, core, t8 @2025-08-04T21:49:00) Maybe not Christmas every year but wants an extra visit if can swing it
[6] (about=Kofi, core, t6 @2025-07-28T22:51:00) Toronto-London flights over Christmas are brutal this year; might be an even year this time
[7] (about=Mum, core, t6 @2025-07-28T22:51:00) Wants everyone home for Christmas; willing to move lunch or do Boxing Day to accommodate Kofi
agent_answer:
- **Mum**: Yes – she states the norm explicitly: “Everyone home, yes?” and “we said everyone.” She wants everyone, including Kofi, home for Christmas.
- **Kofi**: No – he says maybe not Christmas every year; flights are brutal and this might be an “even year” he misses.
- **Dad**: The material doesn’t show him claiming the norm applies or exempting himself; his comment is about not building Christmas around airline pricing.
- **Imogen**: The material shows her accepting Kofi may not come and suggesting a video call, but doesn’t show her rejecting the norm for herself.

So the norm is insisted on by **Mum**, but it is **not uniformly accepted/applied by Kofi**.
